newsitem.title: UK: North Sea, Med crude spreads ease as IPE rebounds.
newsitem.headline: North Sea, Med crude spreads ease as IPE rebounds.

text.p: North Sea crude premiums continued to slide on Friday, despite a strong recovery in Brent IPE futures, traders said.
Mediterranean markets were also weak after five Iraqi crude export contracts were approved by the U.N. on Thursday.
January Brent gained 50 cents to around $23.50 per barrelby 1830 GMT, and the Jan/Feb spread was steady at +40/45 cents.

A Statfjord cargo loading on Dec 24-26 was sold at Dated Brent +18 cents, 18 cents below its level of Wednesday, illustrating the slide in North Sea grade premiums. Oseberg also moved at a weaker number which was kept confidential.
"There is general weakness on the backwardation on Brent, which has made the grades suffer, and there's additional weakness due to some end-of-month barrels still on the market," a trader said.
Dated Brent, as a differentail to Jan Brent paper, tumbled again on Friday to be offered as low as -15 cents, from Jan evens on Thursday and +20 the day before.
Sour Urals crude in the Mediterranean suffered from a lack of buying interest, partially due to the imminent return of Iraq and despite loading delays in Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
A Urals cargo loading over the weekend was looking for bids around Dated Brent -40 cents c+f Augusta, a trader said.
The U.N. in New York said on Thursday night that five contracts for Iraqi crude exports have been approved, and Turkish news agency said the first vessel was due to load from Ceyhan next week.
